newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Stocks likely to hold gains today.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Stocks likely to hold gains today.

text.p: A sell-side imbalance at the opening of trading failed to push the U.S. stock market lower, raising the chances that stocks will end on the plus side, options traders and analysts said Friday.
"With a sell imbalance, there were still plenty of buy orders and the market's been up since the get-go," said Michael Schwartz, a managing director at Oppenheimer & Co.
"Usually the closing imbalance is the same as the opening, but with such an overwhelming offset on the buy side, I've just got to go with a buy imbalance this afternoon."
But come Monday, a correction may set in.
"I think all the fireworks were yesterday, but as for falling apart today, that doesn't look like it's going to happen," said Jay Shartsis at R.F. Lafferty & Co.

But he noted that some sentiment readings remain extremely high and despite gains in some market indexes Friday, small cap stocks, as measured by the Value Line index .VLIC and the Russell 2000 .RUT were down.
"Maybe we start a correction after today," Shartsis said. "That could be."
At 1225 CDT/1725 GMT, the Value Line was down 1.20 at 421.89 and the Russell 2000 was off 2.26 at 394.23.
Opening and closing imbalances are related to the expiration of options on the S&P 500 index and the S&P 100 index.
SPX options finished trading Thursday and expired Friday morning. OEX options finish trading today and expire Saturday.
By 1230 CDT/1730 GMT, the SPX was up 2.26 at 900.25, off its 900.61 intraday high. The OEX was up 3.53 at 877.47 after reaching 877.74.
And the Dow industrial average was ahead 44 points at about 7,821, just a fraction off its intraday high.

Jerry Hegarty, an options analyst at Thomson Financial Services, said in a report that of all the June OEX expirations since 1986, the market has closed in the direction it opened every time except once.
"Whichever way they open seems to be the way they will continue to travel over June expiration days," he said.
In addition, few in-the-money OEX June calls were exercised Thursday, giving some traders another indication that the market may retain the upside into the close.
OEX volume continued to be centered around the at-the-money strikes, the 870s, 875s and 880s.
The OEX June 870 put traded about 15,630 contracts and the 875 put traded 13,320. The 875 call traded 12,545 and the 880 call traded 16,050.
After the expiration, SPX options activity slowed dramatically.
The most active issue was the September 900 put, which traded roughly 2,070 contracts. The July 900 call traded 1,500.
